title: Quick looks: placement and small fixes
wrong: The starting check tests each stage with only two pictures, so one slip or one lucky tap decides a stage. Guided mode (picture kept on) never grows the garden. The screen reader says "1 counters". A review picture in the Empty squares stage has no sign the question changed.
done: The check uses 3 pictures per stage and a 4th only when exactly 2 of 3 are right, so 3 of 4 passes. Plants grow a little in guided mode but never reach In flower. The label says "1 counter and 4 empty squares". Review pictures start with "A look back."
why: Learning design rule 6 says move a child up on mastery, not one lucky answer, and Quick looks' check is the named example. Children who need the picture kept on should still see growth. Screen-reader children need a correct sentence.

title: Hear the question again
wrong: Hop and Pipi have no "Hear it again" button. Tūī drops the voice for the numbers at its lowest help levels, so a child who cannot read the numbers hears only "How many?".
done: Hop and Pipi show a Hear it again button that says the question or the why-line again. Tūī says the full sum or story at every help level, and its button says it too. No new voice recordings are needed.
why: Learning design rule 2 (voice first, Hear it again always visible) and rule 5 (help fades pictures, not the voice for children who cannot read yet).

title: Older games: Show me first for each new kind
wrong: New question kinds (hop back, count back, from 3, altogether, two tides, halves, near doubles, fair or not, ways, empty squares) appear with no demo.
done: The first time a child meets each new kind, a demo or guided go shows it. The server remembers it was seen.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 4: help arrives by itself the first time a new kind appears.

title: Older games: Now you try asks a sister question
wrong: Now you try asks the same question again, so the child can copy the answer. Tūī praises a redo like a first try.
done: Now you try asks a sister question with different numbers. Tūī gives a plain line for a redo.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 7: after show-why the child must work it out, not copy.

title: Honest finish words and praise about the strategy, older games
wrong: The finish screen says "Well done!" however the day went, even after 9 wrong of 10, and level-up lines praise ability. Pipi never says what is next.
done: Finish words change with how many goes were right first time (strong, middle, tricky), level-up lines praise practice, the reward is still paid, and Pipi points on to Kiwi's Beanstalk.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 7: praise the strategy, not cleverness, and be honest, while the day still counts for young children.

title: Save and show the kind of mistake (rule 9)
wrong: Games know the kind of wrong answer but most never save it and no teacher page shows it. Beanstalk files all bonds to 100 under one key.
done: Every game's pupil page shows the child's usual slip in plain words once there is enough evidence, and Beanstalk keeps one key per pair with old keys still working.
why: LEARNING-DESIGN rule 9: record the kind of wrong choice and show it to the teacher so they know what to teach.

title: Help per kind of go in Tūī and Beanstalk
wrong: Both games keep one help level for the whole child, so one new or hard kind of go changes help for all kinds, and Tūī has no three-wrong-in-a-row boost.
done: Tūī keeps help per way of asking and Beanstalk per kind of go (pairs, missing leaf); new kinds start with full help while old ones fade; three wrong first taps in a row give full help for the rest of the round.
why: Help should follow what the child can do on each kind of go, so strong kinds fade sooner and a new kind gets full help.

title: Small fixes in Weka, Tūī, Penguin Pairs and Pipi
wrong: Weka's pebble step needs a Check tap and its split steps only say Try again; Tūī's start step ignores ten-less facts and has dead code; Penguin Pairs' fair-or-not is wordy; Pipi can offer a shell bigger than the whole.
done: Weka finishes a right pebble count by itself, says why on a wrong split number and skips pebbles after a quick right answer; Tūī starts by both kinds of fact and the dead code is gone; fair or not has two plain choices; Pipi shells never exceed the whole.
why: Each makes a go clearer or shorter and stops guessing or silly choices from hiding what a child knows.
